title: Bayesian ML & Probabilistic Programming
tagline: Reason with uncertainty: priors and posteriors, MCMC, PyMC, hierarchical models, Gaussian processes, variational inference, and Bayesian deep learning.
prereqs: Machine Learning and Math for ML, Deeper (probability distributions, MLE, the multivariate Gaussian, KL divergence).

steps.title: Probabilities of probabilities
steps.why: Treat an unknown rate as something you can be uncertain about.

steps.title: Bayesian updating by counting
steps.why: McElreath builds a posterior from counted ways the data could occur.

steps.title: Conjugate priors
steps.why: Update a Beta prior with data in closed form.

steps.title: MLE vs MAP
steps.why: How adding a prior turns maximum likelihood into MAP.

steps.title: Bayesian linear regression
steps.why: Regression with a distribution over weights, not one answer.

steps.title: Markov chain Monte Carlo
steps.why: Sample a posterior known only up to its normalizing constant.

steps.title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
steps.why: Use gradients to make big, efficient sampler moves.

steps.title: Bayesian modeling with PyMC
steps.why: Write a model in Python and let PyMC sample it.

steps.title: Posterior predictive checks
steps.why: Simulate fake data from the model to see if it fits.

steps.title: Hierarchical models
steps.why: Share strength across groups with partial pooling.

steps.title: Gaussian processes
steps.why: A prior over whole functions, with error bars for free.

steps.title: Bayesian optimization
steps.why: Tune expensive black boxes with a GP and an acquisition function.

steps.title: Variational inference and the ELBO
steps.why: Turn inference into optimization when sampling is too slow.

steps.title: Bayesian neural networks
steps.why: Get uncertainty estimates out of deep networks.

projects: Estimate a coin's bias three ways (grid, conjugate Beta update, and PyMC) and plot the three posteriors together.
Fit a hierarchical PyMC model to per-group data (e.g. ratings by restaurant) and compare it with no pooling and full pooling.
Use Bayesian optimization to tune two hyperparameters of a scikit-learn model and compare it with random search.
